transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jules Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Anil Verma (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Aurora Head of Search), Devon Lee (Aurora Staff ML Eng), Omar Khan (Aurora CTO), Kelly (PM)

Summary (auto): Discuss throughput targets, hosting tradeoffs, and rerank architecture. Action items listed separately.

00:00:05 Jules: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jules from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Quick round of intros?
00:00:11 Marta: Hi, Marta Ruiz, head of search at Aurora. We're looking at improving relevance and reducing latency for results on our analytics platform.
00:00:18 Devon: Devon here, staff ML engineer, I own vector infra and the Milvus cluster.
00:00:22 Omar: Omar, CTO, I'll be listening in for compliance and cost impact.
00:00:27 Kelly: Kelly, PM.
00:00:30 Jules: Awesome. Priya and Anil from our SE org will help with the tech details. Priya, quick intro?
00:00:36 Priya: Hi all, Priya Nambiar, I focus on high-throughput embedding pipelines and rerank integration.
00:00:41 Anil: Anil Verma, I look after private deployments and VPC/on-prem options.
00:00:46 Jules: Great. Quick agenda: understand your current stack, QPS and tail-latency SLOs, embedding dims and vector DB, and then walk options: hosted, dedicated, private.

00:01:05 Marta: To kick things off, our current prod load is about 150 qps average for search traffic, peaks up to 220 qps during business hours. We do a hybrid flow: first embed + topK fanout from Milvus, then a rerank step where we call an LLM to score the top 20. We're trying to reduce cost and tail-latency.
00:01:28 Devon: We're on Milvus 2.x, sharded across 6 nodes. Embeddings are 1536 dims currently, using OpenAI embeddings historically but looking to move to an in-house FT model and maybe switch provider.
00:01:41 Priya: OK, good context. When you say rerank top 20 with an LLM, are you doing full generation for each candidate or a single batch call that scores them?
00:01:49 Devon: Right now it's a per-candidate score call, which is messy. We want to move to batch rerank where possible.
00:01:55 Priya: Makes sense. Redwood supports both approaches. For cost and tail-latency we often recommend batching the rerank call if candidates are small and the prompt fits. With our dedicated pools you can get predictable throughput to support batched scoring of 20 items in a single request.

00:02:20 Omar: Our compliance ask: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and the ability to keep embeddings in our VPC for residency. Also KMS for key management. Which hosting options support that?
00:02:31 Anil: For full control, Redwood Private with VPC connectors or our on-prem package meets residency and KMS/HSM requirements. Dedicated offers reserved capacity with VPC peering and customer-managed keys for many customers; hosted is faster to start but has more constraints around strict data residency.
00:02:50 Marta: Cost-wise we're sensitive. Dedicated seems expensive if we underutilize capacity. Are there burst or autoscale options?
00:02:58 Priya: Yes, dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity. You can also mix: run embeddings hosted and rerank on dedicated, or use caching to reduce calls to the rerank path.

00:03:20 Devon: About embedding dims: 1536 is expensive in storage and vector DB cost. If we reduce to 768 or quantize, what's the accuracy drop? And how does that change runtime on Redwood?
00:03:33 Priya: Typical fidelity vs throughput tradeoff: going from 1536 to 768 dims often reduces storage and vector DB fanout cost by roughly half, with some drop in recall depending on model and tasks. On Redwood, smaller dims reduce tokenization and KV cache overhead slightly but the big win is smaller vectors in your vdb. We also recommend running a small eval set to quantify recall loss. For throughput, dedicated serves tokens faster due to GPU pooling; embedding generation cost scales with model size, so quantized or smaller models help.

00:04:07 Marta: We're also looking at hybrid search: dense + lexical signals. We want to keep BM25 in the loop and only rerank when necessary. Any guidance?
00:04:15 Priya: That's pretty standard. Use a hybrid re-ranker where you do lexical to shortlist, then embed rerank. Redwood's routing can execute fallbacks: if dedicated pool is busy, we can route to a cheaper hosted model variant. For hybrid thresholding, set confidence cutoffs so you don't call the reranker for high BM25-scored docs.

00:04:40 Devon: Can you integrate with Milvus natively? We currently host Milvus ourselves.
00:04:44 Anil: Yes, customers integrate Redwood embeddings with existing vector DBs. We provide SDKs and examples for Milvus, Faiss, and Pinecone. Common pattern: generate embeddings in Redwood or user-side, push to Milvus, then call Redwood rerank with ids and metadata. There's also an option to host both embedding gen and rerank in the same private cluster to avoid egress.

00:05:06 Kelly: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching for rerank? We sometimes have repeated queries which could benefit from caching.
00:05:12 Priya: Redwood supports prefix/KV cache for generation responses; for rerank we support caching of rerank responses keyed by top-K IDs + query hash. That significantly reduces calls for repeated similar queries. Cache TTL and invalidation can be configured per-route.

00:05:35 Omar: Latency SLOs: we need p95 under 200ms for user-facing search. Is that realistic if we do embed+fanout+rerank?
00:05:45 Priya: It's tight. Typical split: embedding gen 20-50ms (if warmed), vector DB fanout 20-80ms depending on shards and locality, rerank 50-200ms depending on model and batching strategy. For p95 under 200ms you likely need to: 1) pre-generate embeddings for queries where possible, 2) use smaller rerank models or batch scoring, 3) co-locate rerank near your Milvus cluster (private/dedicated) or use caching.

00:06:18 Devon: We get heavy tail due to lockstep spikes. How's queuing handled in dedicated pools?
00:06:24 Priya: Dedicated capacity gives you a reserved number of concurrent workers; you can set autoscale with queue sizing and burst rules. If the queue grows, our smart routing can failover to hosted variants instead of dropping requests.

00:06:38 Marta: Any numbers you can share for throughput? Like tokens/s or requests/s for a typical GPU profile?
00:06:43 Anil: For a single A100-like worker serving a 7B reranker model quantized, you might get several hundred small scoring calls per second if batched. For larger models or for unbatched per-candidate scoring, throughput is much lower. We'll share benchmark sheets.

00:07:00 Devon: We also need to avoid double egress costs if we route between our VPC and hosted. If we run Redwood Private, do you support an on-prem deployment that sits entirely inside our network?
00:07:10 Anil: Yes, on-prem package supports air-gapped or private deployments. That includes our orchestration and runtime, and you can keep vectors and keys local. It's heavier to operate but meets strict residency.

00:07:25 Kelly: What's the fastest path to test? We want to see cost delta and latency tradeoffs fast.
00:07:31 Jules: Two-step: 1) quick POC on hosted: Redwood generates embeddings via hosted API and you load them into Milvus; run rerank with hosted model for baseline. 2) Parallel pilot on dedicated with small reserved pool to test p95 and throughput. That gives apples-to-apples metrics.

00:07:49 Devon: For the POC, sample dataset will be 10k queries and 1M doc vectors. Peak QPS simulated at 250. Is that doable?
00:07:57 Priya: Yes we can run that. We'll provide a benchmark template and a small runner script. For 1M vectors at 1536 dims, expect Milvus cost to be notable; we'll include dimension-reduced tests and quantization variants in the benchmark.
00:08:15 Marta: Are there any gotchas with Milvus indexing types? We use HNSW for recall but it affects fanout latency.
00:08:22 Priya: Right — HNSW gives faster queries but index build/maintenance times differ. For heavy write throughput you'll want to test insertion patterns. Also sharding and replica placement impact tail latency. We'll include index tuning tips in the doc we share.

00:08:42 Omar: Security — SAML and audit logs are must-haves. Also, can you instrument per-request tracing into our observability stacks?
00:08:51 Anil: Yes, Redwood Console supports tracing hooks and export of traces/metrics to common sinks. Audit logs and per-request metadata can be pushed to your SIEM via tenant retention options.

00:09:05 Devon: One more: rerank prompt stability. We're worried about output drift and model regression when we update models.
00:09:12 Priya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals. You can pin model versions per-route and do canary rollouts to detect regressions before full cutover.

00:09:26 Marta: Sounds good. On the cost question, do you have an example TCO for Hosted vs Dedicated for our profile?
00:09:33 Jules: We'll create a TCO that shows per-token cost, reserved GPU cost, and estimated vector DB costs for dims 1536 vs 768 and quantized 512 variants. We'll also show a hybrid approach of hosted embeddings + dedicated rerank to balance cost and latency.

00:09:51 Kelly: Great. Any questions from your side, Devon?
00:09:55 Devon: How do you do model pinning and rollbacks? If we discover a quality regression are rollbacks instant?
00:10:02 Priya: You can pin to model commit hashes and roll back to prior model versions. With canary rollouts you can send X% of traffic to the new model and measure. Rollbacks are immediate in the control plane; in-flight requests may still finish on older workers depending on routing but from a control surface it's quick.

00:10:20 Marta: I'm trying to think of stakeholders — security, infra, product. We'll need the whole package before we present to procurement.

00:10:28 Jules: Understood. We'll send SOC2, SSO guides, KMS integration steps, and a short architecture note describing dedicated vs private options.

00:10:38 Omar: What's typical SLA for dedicated customers?
00:10:42 Anil: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets vary by contract tier. For most enterprise dedicated customers it's 99.9% with latency SLOs defined per-route; we'll surface that in the contract discussion.

00:10:56 Kelly: Any recommended model sizes for rerank? We're balancing quality vs tokens.
00:11:01 Priya: Small rerank models (3-7B) can be surprisingly good if you fine-tune or use instruction-tuned rerank heads. For the highest quality, ensemble approaches or 13B+ could be used for offline re-ranking. For user-facing p95 under 200ms, stick to lighter rerank models and batch scoring.

00:11:21 Devon: About batching: if we batch 20 candidates into one rerank call, that reduces the number of model invocations but increases single-call latency; have you seen p95 improvements overall?
00:11:30 Priya: Generally yes. Effective throughput improves since GPUs prefer fewer larger batches. The tradeoff is p99 tail for a single call can be higher, so it depends on your SLO. We'll include benchmarking guidance for batch sizes.

00:11:49 Marta: Anything else on vector DB fallback strategies?
00:11:52 Anil: We recommend a fallback hierarchy: 1) local cache, 2) Milvus primary, 3) replicated read-only region, 4) degrade to lexical-only if no vectors available. Redwood's routing layer can orchestrate that.

00:12:10 Jules: OK let's surface next steps and owners.
00:12:14 Jules: Action items recap: Jules to send pricing/TCO and docs by Friday, Priya to send benchmark template and schedule tech deep dive, Devon to share sample dataset and qps profile, Marta to confirm compliance stakeholders.
00:12:28 Marta: Sounds good. Quick clarifying q: when you say dedicated reserved pool, can we start with a very small pool and scale up?
00:12:36 Anil: Yes, start minimal and configure autoscale/burst. We can set up policy to scale based on queue depth or latency.

00:12:46 Kelly: Timeline — we want a POC in the next 3 weeks. Is that realistic?
00:12:51 Jules: Yes, POC kickoff this month. We'll aim for a 2-3 week pilot window for the initial benchmark.

00:12:58 Devon: One small nit: when you send the benchmark runner, include instructions for Milvus index settings so our results are comparable.
00:13:05 Priya: Will do. We'll include index configs, recommended HNSW params, and quantization settings.

00:13:15 Omar: Thanks, all. No more questions from me right now.
00:13:19 Jules: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.

00:13:25 Speaker 1: (unintelligible) okay thanks.
00:13:30 Meeting ends

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions around technical acronyms (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache), some speaker label noise near end.
notes: Customer prefers a hybrid approach: hosted embeddings for cost, dedicated for rerank. Benchmarks to include dims 1536/768/512 quantized and batch sizes of 1/10/20. Include Milvus index configs and SOC2/KMS docs.
